paragraphs.text: Wake the agent when a directory changes, with the diff and without the echo of its own writes.
# dsh-folderwatch
**Wake the agent when the filesystem changes — not when you remember to look.**
An agent can already be woken on a clock (scheduled tasks) and on an HTTP request (webhooks). Neithe
r covers the case that actually matters mid-session: something *outside* the conversation touches a
file. A build finishes. A formatter rewrites the tree. A test runner drops a report. A download land
s. A colleague pushes into a shared folder. Today the agent finds out only if it happens to look.
`dsh-folderwatch` arms a directory against the agent that armed it. When the tree changes, the agent
receives an exact account of what changed — and can either be woken to act on it or simply find it
waiting at its next step.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why it is not just `fs.watch` and a callback
Three decisions separate a watcher you keep armed from one you uninstall after an afternoon:
### 1. Snapshots, not raw events
`fs.watch` reports that *something* happened, not *what*. It double-fires on Windows, sometimes repo
rts no filename at all, and silently drops events under load. A watcher built directly on it tells t
he agent "something changed" — which is not enough to act on.
This plugin takes **snapshots and diffs them**. Renames, deletions and bursts are classified correct
ly on every platform, and each change arrives with its size. `fs.watch` is kept only as a *hint to r
escan sooner*; the periodic rescan is the correctness path.
### 2. Echo suppression
A watcher on a directory the agent is editing has an obvious failure mode. The agent writes `src/app
.ts`, the watcher fires, the agent is told `src/app.ts` changed, it reads the file it just wrote. Th
at one settles — but a build, a formatter or a test runner the agent *itself* started keeps writing,
and each write wakes the agent again. The result is a loop that burns tokens and reads as if the wo
rkspace were under attack by a stranger.
So tool calls that name a file are recorded in a short-lived ledger, and changes to those paths insi
de the window are counted as **suppressed** rather than delivered. The window is deliberately short
(`echoWindowMs`, default 2500ms): a file the agent wrote ten minutes ago changing *now* is real news
`echoWindowMs`, default 2500ms): a file the agent wrote ten minutes ago changing *now* is real news.
The suppression is visible rather than silent — every batch reports how many events it filtered, so
you can tell "nothing happened" from "the agent did it itself".
### 3. Delivery is opt-in per watch
| mode | call | effect |

| `wake` *(default)* | `agent.followup(message)` | starts a new turn |
| `queue` | `agent.inject(mes
sage)` | waits for the agent's next step |
A watcher that can always interrupt is a watcher nobody leaves armed. The quieter option is one argu
ment away, so you can arm a watch for a whole session without handing it the power to interrupt you.

The package declares no `dsh-*` peer dependency on purpose: it imports only `node:*` plus `@deepseek
-ai/dsh-tools`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`, all of which the harness reso
lves from its own installation. Nothing is bundled that could shadow the host's copy.
To tune it per profile, add a `config` block to the row the installer inserted in `~/.dsh/profiles/<
profile>/cordis.patch.yml`:

## Tools
### `folderwatch_add`
Arm a watch. Returns the arm report, or the reason it could not be armed.
| argument | type | meaning |

| `path` | string *(required)* | Directory to watch. Absolute, or relative to the workspace. |
| `la

bel` | string | Short name shown in listings and notifications. |
| `prompt` | string | Instruction

appended to each notification, e.g. `re-run the failing test`. |
| `pattern` | string | Glob selecti

ng which paths are reported, e.g. `**/*.log`. |
| `ignore` | string[] | Extra ignore patterns for th

is watch. A bare name like `tmp` matches at any depth. |
| `recursive` | boolean | Descend into subd

irectories. Defaults to `true`. |
| `once` | boolean | Disarm after the first delivery. Defaults to

`false`. |
| `mode` | `"wake"` \| `"queue"` | Delivery mode. Defaults to `wake`. |
| `sessionId` | s
tring | Session to notify, when it is not the calling one. |
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### `folderwatch_list`
The inventory: what each watch is watching, how often it has fired, and whether anything is pending.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### `folderwatch_check`
Rescan now and report what changed **without delivering a message**. This is how you answer "has any
thing happened yet" during a turn instead of waiting to be woken.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### `folderwatch_fire`
Deliver a watch's pending changes immediately instead of waiting for the quiet period. Useful to con
firm the delivery path works, or when a batch is known to be complete. When nothing is pending, it s
ays so and sends nothing.
### `folderwatch_remove`
Disarm a watch and release its filesystem handles. Reports what it delivered while armed.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
